record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is the polynomial-time class P-TIME equal to DLOG, the class DSPACE(log n) of languages decidable by deterministic logarithmic-space Turing machines?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{P}$ denote the class of all languages $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ decidable by some deterministic Turing machine running in time $n^{O(1)}$ on inputs of length $n$. Let $\mathrm{L} = \mathrm{DSPACE}(\log n)$ denote the class of all languages decidable by some deterministic Turing machine that, on inputs of length $n$, uses at most $O(\log n)$ cells on its work tapes (the input tape being read-only and not counted toward the space bound). It is known that $\mathrm{L} \subseteq \mathrm{P}$.

Determine whether $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{L}$, i.e., whether every language decidable in deterministic polynomial time is also decidable in deterministic logarithmic space.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether $\mathrm{L} = \mathrm{P}$ is a long-standing major open problem in computational complexity theory; no proof of equality or separation is known as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: L (complexity) — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is unknown whether L = P, and resolving this is a major open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The equality L = P is still open.

status_evidence.title: Complexity Zoo: L
status_evidence.snippet: Whether L = P is one of the great open problems of complexity theory.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference lists L vs P as open.
